thread.title: Redfin: The 'Everything' Of Real Estate - Redfin (NASDAQ:RDFN) | Seeking Alpha

author: Maks F. S.
title: Redfin: The 'Everything' Of Real Estate - Redfin (NASDAQ:RDFN) | Seeking Alpha
text:
Woohoo! We just closed on our transaction as buyers through Redfin!
As many of my long time readers know, I generally focus on analyzing income focused investments, namely closed end funds and ETFs. The small list of equities which I discuss are only companies of which I am a customer, client or an end user of, or in industries where I have direct experience either from my earlier career or working with today.
Redfin ( RDFN ) is a company which I have heard about for many years from my numerous colleagues and business partners in the real estate and mortgage industries. It was not until last fall however that I decided to experience what it was like to be a Redfin customer.
From my very first time of browsing for homes in the app, to scheduling a showing for later that day and then having lengthy discussions with the local Redfin lead agent, I realize that this was something truly unique, as unique as the very first time you found out you can go to Amazon.com, buy whatever you need at very low prices and then having it delivered in a day or so, and then later finding out that Amazon ( AMZN ) would deliver thousands of products to your door step the very same day.
It was because of that experience that I started researching Redfin's financials and business concept to figure out if it is a worthy investment. That lead me to writing my initial and follow up articles on the company, " Redfin: Another 'Great Company, But Horrible Stock'? " and " Redfin: 'Amazon' Of Real Estate? "
Since my last article we have closed on our home and in the process used two of Redfin' services. With that completed, let's discuss why I believe any investor should not dismiss the company as "yet another tech startup" and why real estate investors need to seriously consider having exposure to this yet largely un-noticed investment.
Not Inventing Real Estate Amazon did not invent the book selling or delivery business. Apple ( AAPL ) did not invent cell phones. Starbucks ( SBUX ) did not invent coffee.
What those companies did however was to take existing businesses, identified the pain points, and then created solutions which addressed those issues.
In that light, Redfin is not inventing real estate, the concept real estate as an investment, the real estate brokerage model, or the real estate settlement and mortgage businesses. What they are doing is creating solutions which address the major problems being identified by both buyers and sellers of real estate.
As such, even though Redfin is by all means a tech start up, they do not have to prove the vast majority of the business models as those models have generally worked over the past 100 years or more!
For those reasons the company is not taking on the risk of creating a Segway (those things mall cops ride), virtual or augmented reality products such as Nintendo ( OTCPK:NTDOY ) Virtual Boy or Google ( GOOG ) Glass, or the Sony Betamax. We can also say that Redfin is not creating anything new consumer fads "de jour" such as personal fitness tracker bands like the Fitbit ( FIT ) and to the lesser extent personal video cameras such as GoPros ( GPRO ) and dedicated e-book readers such as the Amazon Kindle or the Barnes & Noble ( BN ) Nook.
Real estate is not a fad and until humanity learns to ascend to the next level of evolution into energy and shed our physical forms (shout out to all Stargate fans), we will need a place to live, and for most that will the sale or a purchase of a home. (yes yes yes.... tongue in cheek, let the author have some humor.)
Redfin is simply making real estate and the real estate transaction process significantly less stressful and costly and displacing the existing "business as usual" incumbents in the process. This is why I believe this is the best form of tech investing, Redfin is innovating rather than re-inventing. This is far less risky than going out to market to create a brand new product with an unproven business model.
Multiple Revenue Sources Certainly one of the most exciting prospects for the company as an investment is the multiple revenue sources.
Brokerage - At the core of the business is of course the commission tied to the purchase and sale of the home. Here, Redfin operates on the same 6% to 8% of the purchase price as their Realogy ( RLGY ) and Re/Max ( RMAX ) peers do. The difference here is that on transactions where Redfin represents the seller, the company is only charging 1% to 1.5% as opposed to the typical 3% to 4%. On transactions where Redfin represents the buyer, the company is taking their commission and splitting a portion of that fee with the buyers in the form of a refund (where allowed). So while Redfin competes directly with their national and local rivals, the company does offer a competitive advantage to its buyers and sellers in the form of a refund or a lower sales commission.
Source: Title Forward
Settlement Services - In most real estate transactions, especially those involving a mortgage, you will need the services of either an attorney or a settlement company to close the transaction along with in most cases, title insurance. Redfin has an affiliated title and settlement company, Title Forward which is currently operating in about 13 states. While there is far less revenue generated by title insurance and settlement services, I also believe there is a very high conversion factor for Redfin customers to also use Title Forward. The reason is simple..., while quite a few customers may have an existing mortgage broker relationship, very few know of, or care about who their settlement and title insurance provider is. From our personal perspective, having used Title Forward for our insurance and settlement, we found the process very streamlined as there was transparent information sharing between the brokerage and settlement side in the form of Redfin's virtual "Deal Room." As this is rolled out in more markets, this will most certainly add additional revenues.
Source: Redfin Mortgage
Mortgage Originations - Beside the sales commission, the other large source of revenue is the mortgage. While as a financial professional I have numerous mortgage contacts, the majority of real estate buyers likely do not. While there is exceptionally strong competition for the mortgage lending, I firmly believe that given the choice, after starting the Redfin house search, a good amount of shoppers would choose to get their mortgage from Redfin, especially due to their 30 day closing guarantee. While the company has not yet reported any meaningful revenue here, Redfin Mortgage is only available in a few states, Georgia, Illinois, Minnesota, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas, Virginia, and Washington D.C. As the company expands its presence and starts taking more active efforts of pushing Redfin Mortgage, it has the potential to become the next "Rocket Mortgage" with a captive and willing prospect base.
Concierge Services - The company also offers a more proactive, hands on selling service called Redfin Concierge. While the 1% covers its listing fee, for a higher sales commission Redfin takes a more proactive and hands on approach with your home. For the addition 1% or so, the company will deep clean, declutter and stage your home, in an effort to sell your home faster and for more money. There are two ways investors can look at this. The first is as a competitive advantage where for essentially the "regular" sales commission, Redfin is going to do A LOT MORE to get it sold. The second way of looking at Redfin Concierge is as a way of tapping into and capturing some of the "sale preparation" marketplace for services such as staging and photography.
Source: Redfin
Real Estate Investing - Technology companies like Google are known for experimentation and Redfin is no different. The company recently launched their Redfin Now home buying service. In an effort to generate more revenue, the company is heading into the real estate investor territory now made popular by the "Cash For Your Home" industry. Currently, the "cash for home" industry is made up of investors, both big and small who will make you a guaranteed offer on your house, generally at a far lower price in the hopes of immediately flipping it or renovating and flipping your home at a higher price. What is interesting to see is whether Redfin, merely due to their wealth of data, can make more informed buy and sell decisions compared to their incumbent competitors. What will be further interesting to see is if Zillow's similar recent efforts will also work out.
Source: Redfin
The Un-Monetized 800 lb Gorilla In The Room What I believe is still the yet largely overlooked aspect of the company which also has the potential of being the biggest source of revenue in the future is the large and growing amount of data and analytics being generated and analyzed by Redfin.
As the industry is highly fragmented, many parties have copious data on specific parts of the real estate market. Redfin however has data starting from when someone downloads the app and starts looking for a home up until they close and take possession of the property.
While many would have found the HAL 9000 a bit creepy, we are now living in the world where Google, Amazon, Facebook ( FB ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ) can anticipate what we will want to do, eat or buy.
Redfin can be one of those "Big Data" companies for the real estate industry.
It is true of course that there is already competition from companies such as Zillow ( Z ). The difference here however is that Redfin has a more detailed data set beyond the browsing habits. In that light, the company can largely duplicate what Zillow is doing by meaningfully expanding to selling real estate leads, especially in areas and situations where Redfin agents are already too busy for the existing and growing demand.
One way we can think of this side of the business is much like we did with Facebook ( FB ) and Twitter ( TWTR ) before they started monetizing their data. It may and likely will take some time, however I believe it is a near certainty that people will be using that data and analytics. It may be sold to realtors and industry providers or it just may be used by Redfin internally to help grow Redfin Now through making more informed home buying decisions.
Bottom Line So far, the company seems to elicit either a love it or hate it response.
The vast majority of the feedback and emotion seem to be quite positive, especially amongts millenials on various social media sites such as Reddit.
There are however a constant group of naysayers, likely traditional real estate agents who are quick to dismiss the company as just another "low fee" brokerage with a better app.
It is quite true, Redfin IS a lower fee brokerage model with a FAR BETTER app, but it is also so much more for the reasons I highlighted in this article.
Amazon was also not an instant overnight success and for many many years investors in particular questioned the company operating on razor thin margins and not showing a profit and instead of reinvesting heavily into the business. There were many industry people also using this as an excuse that retail stores would not be impacted as Amazon could not sell their products without a loss. A few years later with a large and growing list of shuttered retailers and the remaining retailers against the ropes, we know who won.
With Redfin, we also have to wait while the company scales up and continues to grow.
In the mean time however, there are a few things we need to keep an eye out on.
First, "Are consumers interested in the company?"
Based on the constantly scheduled agents in the tri-state area, I would say yes. Of course, let's get something more provable.
One of my favorite data points to look at here is the company's Google "search trends" over time.
Source: Google Trends
As we can clearly see, over the last 14 years the interest in the company, and in particular the amount of people search for the company on Google has continued to growth with the regular seasonality of real estate.
This falls in line with the website and app usage figures provided by the company.
What is also interesting to see is that for now, the company is largely recognized in their home state of Washington and in the North West.
Source: Google Trends
As the company continues to grow out in the North East, I believe the financial community will take a serious look once they perhaps themselves, become a Redfin client.
The second factor is whether the company's core business revenue is growing.
RDFN Revenue (NYSE: TTM ) data by YCharts
Yes, it is.
Is the net income growing or for a start up are the losses slowing?
RDFN Net Income ( TTM ) data by YCharts
In general, seems to be. We only have a years worth of data as a public company however the Q over Q net loss shrank.
Bottom line, the business concept makes sense, the customers are extremely happy and now it is just about watching the paint dry as the company continues to make progress.
